summary: Round-1 findings are all addressed correctly. The five fixes (T1 NUL-byte round-trip with literal NUL chars confirmed by `file` reporting the test source as binary `data`; T2 explicit null-IV case plus @ValueSource parameterization over {0,11,13,16}; T3 cause-chain walker replacing stack-trace substring match; T4 deterministic one-bit XOR of the valid IV; T5 @NullAndEmptySource covering both null and "" constructor paths) all pin behaviour rather than implementation detail and survive the litmus test — removing the corresponding production line in each case causes the assertion to fail. The new hexParseErrorMessageDoesNotEchoKeyBytes test correctly pins the security guarantee from the round-1 security audit (no leaked offending byte) using two narrowly-scoped negative substring assertions ('z' and "at index") which both come from the JDK's HexFormat error string, so a future drift back to passing the raw cause message through `getMessage()` would fail; the assertions are tight enough to catch the regression yet do not over-constrain wording of the user-facing message. Cause-chain walker handles the self-cause edge case (`cur.getCause() == cur`) and uses Optional return cleanly. Bonus: the boot-validation test gained a positive happy-path assertion already in round 1 and that remains. No new issues surfaced.
